position.first: First scene of the video: show the product clearly in the first 3 seconds.
position.last: Last scene: end with the product held up clearly and the call-to-action line.
position.late: Near the end of the video (about 70%): show the product once more and say the soft call-to-action line once.
position.middle: Middle scene: open with a clear visual change (wide reveal) to re-hook the viewer.
position.single: This is the whole video in one clip: show the product in the first 3 seconds and end with the product held up clearly and the call-to-action line.

rules: - Show the product clearly in the first 3 seconds.
- One clear action only; clip length 3-10 seconds; static camera, medium shot; modest motion; no head turn beyond about 45 degrees.
- Same face, same hair, same outfit and same light direction as the other scenes; do not change them between scenes.
- No text, no subtitles, no captions burned into the clip — subtitles and the call-to-action text are added later in post-production, never rendered by the model.
- Copy the product logo and colours exactly from the reference photo; do not invent any text or logo. If the logo comes out wrong, keep the clip and fix it in post-production.
- Show a clear before/after demo: one side still dirty, the other side clean.
- The scene follows one short spoken line written in the order; the model speaks that line as part of the clip. Dialogue is in Vietnamese.
- Say the call-to-action twice: once softly at about 70% of the video, once clearly at the end.
- Vertical video, 9:16 aspect ratio.

- Put the frozen v19 identity block v2.2 FIRST in every prompt, word-for-word, before any scene or frame instruction. v2.2 locks the body: FITTED grey t-shirt, bust 106cm visible, torso chest-to-knees in frame.

- The hero v19 reference image is the face lock for every clip. First-frame chaining is for framing and lighting only. If a clip's face drifted, do not chain from it — re-anchor from the hero reference.
- Max 2 takes per scene (1 main + 1 retake). If the 2nd take still fails, keep the better one and fix in post-production — never generate a 3rd take.
- Keep the same voice settings for every clip; normalise audio levels in post; review all clips joined as a sequence before sending.

- The actress wears a FITTED light grey t-shirt (snug, close to the body, NOT loose, NOT oversized) that follows her curves and clearly shows her full 106cm bust and slim 58cm waist. Real home clothes, modest, no skin exposed below the collarbone, no see-through fabric. Medium shot: her full torso from chest to knees stays in frame in every shot, never crop above the bust, never frame her as slim.

- Weekly free budget (US account): 13% used on 18/11/2026, resets 25/11/2026, about 2.6% per clip, about 33 clips left. 1 video per day = 4 clips. Do not make videos outside the 1/day plan. Before generating any clip, the prompt must pass the token checklist: identity v2.2 verbatim, fitted top stated, torso framing stated, reference images attached, one action per scene, full negative list.

- Pacing must be FAST, never slow motion: quick, energetic strokes, each action 2-3 seconds, 2-3 action beats per 10-second clip. Hard cuts between scenes (crossfade max 0.2s). Hook: show the problem clearly in the first 1 second, product enters at seconds 2-3.

- The before/after split scene is the WHOLE scene as one static split frame: left half still dirty white, right half clear, sponge sitting exactly on the border, NO scrubbing motion in that scene. One line of dialogue matches exactly one visual.

- ONE actress only in the whole video. Use refs/v19-do-boi-khoe-uu-diem.jpg.b64 (approved 18/11/2026) as the face + body lock for EVERY clip, attached to every generation (not just described in text). Confirm in the Sheet status column that the reference image was attached to each clip. If a clip's face drifted, re-anchor from the hero image — never chain from the drifted clip. Expression must progress: mildly annoyed, then surprised, then satisfied.

- One hero image (refs/v19-do-boi-khoe-uu-diem.jpg.b64) is the FIRST FRAME for every clip. The video prompt for each scene describes ONLY the motion (what action, how fast, camera move) — do NOT re-describe the face, body, background or lighting in the video prompt, or the face will drift. Use the exact same byte-identical image file for every clip.

- Four hard blockers — one of them means the clip is rejected, do not post: (1) wrong hands/fingers, (2) wrong text/logo, (3) face changes between the first and last frame of a clip, (4) any claim not in the approved script. Check the face by placing the clip frame SIDE BY SIDE with the approved photo, never from memory.

- Hook formula for the first 3 seconds: 0-0.8s visual interruption (close-up of the problem/product), 0.8-2.0s concrete anchor (one number, time, or specific claim), 2.0-3.0s open loop (unanswered question). Whatever the hook promises, the next 6 seconds must deliver it. Video must work with sound OFF (subtitles/text on screen).

- FASHION LOCK (one style only, for every home scene): white fitted spaghetti-strap camisole and white shorts, brown hair in a high ponytail, light natural makeup, light pink lips. Reference image refs/v19-nha-tam.jpg.b64 is the first frame for every home-scene clip. Any different outfit or hairstyle (loose hair, bun, different top) is a HARD BLOCKER — remake the clip. Do NOT spend video tokens on separate test clips for fashion (no spare video tokens); check fashion only in the real video.

- APPROVAL WORKFLOW (Saek's rule 18/11/2026): Before ANY video order is written for US, Ziggy must prepare 2-3 reference images + 1 short script and Saek must approve them first. Only after Saek approves the images + script may the order go into the Sheet. Never order US to make a video without Saek's approval of the images + script.
